summary: Wang Pachow (1918–2012) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied under Yun-shan Tan and served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University.

Wannaporn Rienjang is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at the British Museum, the University of Oxford (Gandhara Connections Project), and Thammasat University.
Warren Cowgill (1929–1985) specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and Yale University (~1952–1957), where he also took up a post in 1956.

Warren Lee Todd works in philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD at Lancaster University under Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad (attested 2012), also studying under Irina Kuznetsova, Peter Harvey, and Chogye Trichen Rinpoche.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University. There, he studied under MA supervisors Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, as well as teachers Phra Sudhivorayan and Phramaha Somjin Sammāpañño.

Wasu Harada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and Koyasan University (MA, 1984), and held posts at Koyasan University, Ryukoku University, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, and Shuchiin University.

Wataru S. Ryose is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances A. Wilson.

Wayne Proudfoot (born 1939) is a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Harvard Divinity School (~1962–1965) and Harvard University (~1965–1972), and held a post at Columbia University from around 1972 to 2018.

Wei Lin, a specialist in Buddhist studies and archaeology, studied at Nanjing University, Peking University, and Ohio State University (PhD under John C. Huntington). He held posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum, Western Michigan, Michigan, and Transylvania University.

Wei-jen Teng works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University (PhD under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil), and held a post at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.
Weirong Shen (born 1962) specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He has held teaching posts at Renmin University of China (~2006) and the University of Hong Kong.
Weiru Guan is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2011) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi.
Wen-ling Jane is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University, where she was supervised by Robert A. F. Thurman and taught by Lobsang Jamspal.

Wenbiao Mai is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kyoto University, the University of Hamburg, and Peking University (PhD). Mai was attested as a guest assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong in 2013.

Wendi L. Adamek specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Stanford University (-1998) and held academic posts at Barnard College (attested 2008) and the University of Calgary (attested 2018).

Wendy Doniger (born 1940) specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Radcliffe, Harvard (under Daniel H. H. Ingalls), and Oxford, and served as Mircea Eliade Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago.
Wenjie Duan (1917–2011) was a Buddhist studies and archaeology scholar who studied at the Central Academy of Fine Arts (~1940–1943). In 1991, he served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy.

Wenjie Qin is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Tu Weiming, also studying under Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.
Werner Abraham (1936–2024) was a linguist who completed his studies at the University of Vienna between 1962 and 1965. In 2002, he held an academic post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.

Wes Borton is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at East Carolina University, where he was taught by Derek F. Maher, and at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).
